What You Will Do Build the Project Controls Function from the Ground Up Create the Project Controls charter, service model, RACI, governance cadence, role definitions, staffing roadmap, consultant support model, standards, templates, and implementation plan for a lean organization. Establish practical processes for schedule development, baseline approval, update cycles, variance analysis, progress measurement, change impact review, recovery planning, and executive reporting. Operate hands-on during the early build-out by developing schedules, reviewing contractor updates, building dashboards, producing reports, and coaching project teams until resources and processes mature. Create consistent progress measurement methods for engineering, procurement, permitting, sitework, construction, commissioning, controls, turnover, and customer delivery milestones. Drive forward-looking forecasting by requiring variance explanations, risk-adjusted milestone projections, recovery actions, accountable owners, and clear decision points. Cost, Cash Flow, and Forecast Integration Partner with Cost Control, Finance, Procurement, and Construction Delivery to connect schedule status with cash flow, commitments, cost-to-complete, contingency drawdown, procurement timing, and executive forecasts. Support earned value, productivity, trend, quantity, and progress-to-cost analysis where useful, without overbuilding systems beyond what the lean organization can maintain. Ensure schedule delays, procurement shifts, recovery plans, and change events are translated into financial, customer, capital deployment, and liquidity-readiness implications. Risk, Issues, Change, and Time Impact Governance Build a practical risk, issue, change, and decision-log framework that identifies schedule threats, documents assumptions, assigns owners, tracks mitigation actions, and escalates unresolved constraints. Establish time impact analysis, schedule fragnet, recovery schedule, delay analysis, and change-impact review standards for owner decisions, contractor changes, customer changes, and executive approvals. Partner with Legal, Commercial, Procurement, Construction, and Cost Control to reduce claims exposure, preserve contract rights, evaluate entitlement, and support fact-based negotiation. Planning and Development (PLaD), Pre-Construction, and Readiness Integration Engage early with Planning and Development (PLaD) and the Pre-Construction team so site diligence, power strategy, permitting, design readiness, procurement timing, early works, logistics, and construction sequencing are reflected in integrated milestone plans. Define project controls inputs required before major governance gates, funding requests, customer commitments, procurement releases, construction mobilization, commissioning windows, and turnover commitments. Support constructability, feasibility, and delivery planning reviews by validating schedule assumptions, critical path logic, constraints, risks, and readiness requirements. Procurement, Vendor, and Commissioning Schedule Integration Integrate long-lead equipment, off-site manufacturing, vendor data, factory testing, logistics, installation windows, energization, L1-L5/IST commissioning, controls validation, and turnover dependencies into baseline schedules. Partner with Procurement, Engineering, Controls, Commissioning & Quality, contractors, vendors, and integrators to identify decision dates, submittal needs, fabrication durations, delivery constraints, inspection points, and schedule risks. Ensure procurement and vendor delays are visible early enough for executives to make informed decisions on acceleration, resequencing, alternate sourcing, customer commitments, and contingency actions. Translate technical schedule and controls issues into plain business language focused on customer commitments, capital timing, schedule certainty, cost exposure, risk, and enterprise value. Tools, Standards, Training, and Continuous Improvement Select, configure, or rationalize project controls tools appropriate for a lean scaling organization, including CPM scheduling, reporting, dashboarding, risk tracking, document integration, and data governance needs. Create standard operating procedures, schedule specifications, reporting templates, KPI definitions, contractor requirements, data quality checks, and training materials that can scale across projects and regions. Establish a lessons-learned feedback loop from active projects, contractor performance, schedule misses, commissioning delays, utility constraints, and customer turnover into future planning and baseline assumptions. Strong technical knowledge of CPM scheduling, baseline development, critical path and float analysis, resource/cost loading, recovery planning, and change/time impact evaluation. Experience leading schedulers, project controls managers, consultants, or cross-functional controls contributors across multiple concurrent projects or a large program. Ability to create order in ambiguous, early-stage, rapidly scaling environments with limited existing process and high expectations for execution speed. Working knowledge of cost control, cash flow, forecasting, earned value, contingency, procurement, risk management, and construction execution. Experience developing executive reports, portfolio dashboards, and decision-oriented materials for senior leadership. review_candidates.description: At Transgrid, we play a crucial role in delivering safe, reliable, and sustainable energy to millions of Australians. Operating over 13,000 km of high-voltage transmission lines and 128 substations across NSW and the ACT, we connect electricity generators to the distribution network—powering homes, businesses, and communities. About The Role As as a Program Coordinator, you will provide high-level administrative, operational and project coordination support to the General Manager of Projects, the Class B Projects team, and the broader Infrastructure Delivery team. You will: Coordinate governance and project activities, including meetings, workshops and project forums, preparing agendas, reports, presentations and minutes. Provide executive, project and operational support across the team, including calendar and travel management, event coordination, project documentation, registers, reporting and records, ensuring information is accurate, accessible and up to date. Facilitate effective project and stakeholder coordination, supporting financial and commercial administration such as procurement, contractor engagement, invoices processing and cost tracking, while acting as a key liaison across internal and external stakeholders to enable clear communication and collaboration. About You You are an organised and proactive person who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys supporting teams to deliver successful project outcomes. To be successful, you will bring: Experience in administrative, project coordination or program support roles, ideally within infrastructure, construction, engineering, utilities or other project-based environments. Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines and stakeholder requirements. Strong written and communication skills, with experience preparing reports, presentations, project documentation and correspondence to a high standard. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint and document management systems, with the ability to quickly adapt to new tools and processes. A current Australian driver’s licence is also required. Reward and Recognition We believe in providing our people with personal, professional, and social benefits so they can deliver their best work each and every day. At Transgrid, you are encouraged to build a career that’s right for you. Our Values Transgrid’s core values encompass safety, achievement, integrity, and service. Prioritising safety above all, the company emphasises making a meaningful impact through achievement, upholding honesty through integrity, and delivering exceptional outcomes for customers and communities through dedicated service. These values are ingrained in the actions and behaviours of Transgrid’s people, who embody them every day. Please note vacancy close dates may be subject to change. We will assess applications as they are received. Closing date 29th September 2026. Transgrid is committed to Health and Safety, the Environment, Equal Employment Opportunity, Diversity and Ethical Practices. All applicants are expected to demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to these areas.
